```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

A nested run returns a `nested_results`, a tibble with one row per outer
fold. This page reads one run from start to finish: the estimate, what
each fold selected, the predictions and the plots.

```{r deps, include = FALSE}
needed <- c("tidymodels", "ranger")
missing_pkgs <- needed[
  !vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
has_deps <- length(missing_pkgs) == 0L
```

```{r deps-notice, eval = !has_deps, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(
  "This page attaches the **tidymodels** packages and fits random forests",
  "with the **ranger** package.",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) {
    sprintf("The **%s** package is not installed here,", missing_pkgs)
  } else {
    sprintf(
      "The **%s** packages are not installed here,",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "** and **")
    )
  },
  "so the rest of this page has been skipped. Install",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) "it" else "them",
  "and rebuild to see it.\n"
)

knitr::knit_exit()
```

```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)
```

## The run

We reuse the design, the random forest and the grid from
`vignette("nested-cv")`. This time a `control_grid()` with
`save_pred = TRUE` keeps each outer fold's predictions on its assessment
rows.

```{r run}
set.seed(1)

folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 5),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

rf <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

wf <- workflow(mpg ~ ., rf)

grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2L, 5L, 8L), min_n = c(2L, 10L))

set.seed(2)

res <- nested_tune_grid(
  wf,
  folds,
  grid = grid,
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

res
```

Each row holds one outer fold's score in `.metrics`, the setting it chose
in `.selected`, and every candidate (setting tried) its inner search
scored in `.inner_metrics`. `?nested_tune_grid` describes each column.

`summary()` says in words how much of the design ran, what each fold
chose, and the estimate.

```{r summary}
summary(res)
```

## The estimate

`collect_metrics()` averages the outer scores. Each mean is the estimate
for the whole procedure (tune, select, fit), and `std_err` is the
standard error of that mean.

```{r collect-metrics}
collect_metrics(res)
```

With `summarize = FALSE`, we get each fold's score instead.

```{r per-fold}
collect_metrics(res, summarize = FALSE)
```

`vignette("estimate")` explains what this number describes and what to
report.

## The selections

`collect_selections()` stacks what each fold chose, with the fold label
beside each row. `agreement()` counts how many folds chose each setting.

```{r selections}
collect_selections(res)

agreement(res)
```

When the folds agree, the data points to one setting. When they split, we
read little into any one choice. The model to deploy comes from
`nested_final_fit()`, which tunes once more on all the data, so its choice
can differ from every fold's. The estimate above is still the number to
report for that model, because the same procedure made it.

`collect_inner_metrics()` stacks the inner scores of every candidate in
every fold. Here is the first fold's RMSE for each candidate, best first.

```{r inner}
collect_inner_metrics(res) |>
  filter(id == "Fold1", .metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

## The predictions

`collect_predictions()` stacks each fold's predictions on its assessment
rows. On this design, every row of the data is predicted once by a model
that did not see it.

```{r predictions, fig.width = 4.5, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Predicted against observed miles per gallon, one point per car, with a dashed line where the two are equal."}
preds <- collect_predictions(res)
preds

ggplot(preds, aes(mpg, .pred)) +
  geom_abline(lty = 2) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_obs_pred()
```

## The plots

`autoplot()` draws the selections by default, one panel per tuned
parameter and one point per outer fold.

```{r autoplot-parameters, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "One panel per tuned parameter, mtry and min_n, with one point per outer fold at the value that fold's inner tuning selected."}
autoplot(res)
```

With `type = "performance"`, it draws each fold's score, with a dashed
line at the estimate.

```{r autoplot-performance, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "One panel per metric, rmse and rsq, with one point per outer fold's score on its assessment rows and a dashed line at the mean across folds."}
autoplot(res, type = "performance")
```

A fold that fails does not stop the run, and the functions above answer
over the folds that completed. `collect_notes()` lists what went wrong in
any fold, one that completed included. `?nested_tune_grid` describes
failed folds and the dplyr verbs that keep the class.
